ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Information-Gain Turn Rewards from Gold Answer Likelihood
PROPOSAL: Define a turn reward as the change in the policy's own log-probability of the ground-truth answer after a tool response, computed with a forced answer prefix, and add it to the outcome reward inside GRPO advantages. Train Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as a search agent on a mix of NQ and HotpotQA training questions with 8 rollouts per query for 600 updates, then evaluate exact match on NQ, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Bamboogle. Run 5 seeds and report validation reward curves, final exact match and the share of turns with positive gain.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; turn reward with the answer prefix shuffled between queries; turn reward replacing the outcome reward; turn reward with a fixed small weight.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Information-gain rewards raise exact match over outcome-only GRPO on multi-hop sets and speed early learning. It fails if shuffled-prefix rewards do as well, showing that any shaped signal helps and the answer anchoring does not.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gold-Answer Likelihood Gain as Turn Reward, Compared on Different Backbones
PROPOSAL: Use the change in the policy's log-probability of the ground-truth answer after a tool response, computed by appending a forced answer prefix, as a per-turn term in the GRPO advantage. Train Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct search agents on NQ and HotpotQA training questions with 16 rollouts per query, and evaluate exact match on NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique and Bamboogle. Run 3 seeds and report validation curves, final exact match, and the share of turns with positive gain. Compare the share of positive-gain turns between the two backbones.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; turn reward with the answer prefix shuffled between queries; turn reward replacing the outcome reward; turn reward with a small fixed weight.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Gold-answer gain rewards lift exact match over outcome-only GRPO at both sizes, with the larger relative lift on the smaller model. It fails if the two sizes show the same lift, which would make the size comparison uninformative.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-Level Advantages Restore Gradients When All Rollouts Agree
PROPOSAL: Take 1000 training queries on which Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct produces uniform outcomes over 8 rollouts, and train with GRPO plus a turn reward based on the gain in answer log-probability. Count the fraction of queries with a nonzero advantage, gradient norm per update, and exact match on HotpotQA and 2WikiMultiHopQA dev sets after training. Compare against outcome-only GRPO, using 3 seeds, to check that the turn reward restores gradients on uniform groups without shifting the gradient toward noise.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO on the same queries; outcome GRPO with a larger group size of 16; turn reward with random values of matching variance; training on mixed-outcome queries only.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Turn rewards keep a nonzero advantage on nearly all uniform groups and improve exact match over outcome-only GRPO on those queries. It fails if random-valued rewards give similar gains, which would mean the benefit comes from added noise and not information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Group Size and Turn Rewards in Search Agent Training
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as a search agent on NQ and HotpotQA training queries with GRPO and a turn reward from the gain in answer log-probability, at group sizes 4, 8 and 16 for 5 seeds apiece. Count the fraction of queries with a nonzero advantage, gradient norm per update, and exact match on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Musique dev sets. Compare against outcome-only GRPO at the same group sizes, and fit the relation between group size and the fraction of uniform-outcome queries on all training queries.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO at the same group sizes; turn reward with random values of matching variance; training on mixed-outcome queries only; a turn reward at half weight.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Turn rewards make the result less dependent on group size, with the biggest gain at group size 4 where uniform groups are common. It fails if outcome-only GRPO at group size 16 matches the turn-reward runs, showing group size alone suffices.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn-Level Credit Assignment Probe on Corrupted Trajectories
PROPOSAL: Test whether the turn reward ranks productive turns above unproductive ones by taking 2000 trajectories from a trained Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct search agent and corrupting the turn at position 2, either by swapping its search query for an unrelated one or by deleting the tool response. Score the turn reward on all turns before and after corruption, and report how often the corrupted turn gets the lowest reward in the trajectory and how the final outcome changes. Then train agents with and without the turn reward on NQ and HotpotQA with 3 seeds and compare exact match.
CONTROLS: Outcome reward only, which cannot rank turns; random turn scores; turn score from query length; turn score from retrieved passage overlap with the gold answer string.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The corrupted turn receives the lowest reward in most trajectories and the trained agent improves on HotpotQA over outcome-only training. It fails if passage overlap with the gold string ranks turns as well, which would suggest a cheaper signal does the same job.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Marginal Turn Contribution Estimated from Answer Likelihood Differences
PROPOSAL: Estimate the contribution of a turn by comparing the policy's log-probability of the ground-truth answer with and without the turn, for 5000 trajectories from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct search agents. Check the estimates by corrupting turns with unrelated queries, and report how often the corrupted turn gets the lowest score and how the outcome changes. Then train agents with the estimate as a turn reward on NQ and HotpotQA, 5 seeds per backbone, and compare exact match on the test benchmarks with outcome-only training.
CONTROLS: Outcome reward only, which cannot rank turns; random turn scores; turn score from query length; turn score from passage overlap with the gold answer string.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Corrupted turns receive the lowest score in most trajectories and training with the estimate beats outcome-only training on multi-hop sets. It fails if the leave-one-turn-out estimate behaves like the cheaper log-probability change, which would show the added computation buys nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample Efficiency of Turn-Level Rewards on HotpotQA
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct as a search agent with GRPO and a turn reward based on answer log-probability gain, and with outcome-only GRPO, on HotpotQA training questions with 8 rollouts per query. Log the number of rollouts needed to reach 35, 40 and 45 exact match on the HotpotQA dev set, with 5 seeds per method. Report the ratio of rollouts needed, the area under the validation curve, and exact match on 2WikiMultiHopQA as a transfer check. Training stops at 300 updates for both methods.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; turn reward with half the weight; turn reward with double the weight; a variant with outcome reward normalised by trajectory length.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The turn reward reaches the exact match thresholds with a smaller share of the rollouts, with the biggest saving at the lowest threshold. It fails if the curves overlap after the first updates, which would mean sample efficiency is unchanged.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sample Efficiency of Turn Rewards on Three Training Mixtures
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as a search agent with GRPO, with and without a turn reward from answer log-probability gain, on NQ alone, HotpotQA alone and a mix of both, with 8 rollouts per query and 3 seeds. Log the rollouts needed to reach 35, 40 and 45 exact match on matching dev sets and report the ratio, the area under the validation curve, and transfer exact match on 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique and Bamboogle after 1000 updates. Compare the sample efficiency ratio for the three mixtures.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; turn reward at half weight; turn reward at double weight; outcome reward normalised by trajectory length.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The turn reward saves rollouts on all three mixtures, with the biggest saving on the mix where questions differ in difficulty. It fails if savings vanish for NQ alone, which would limit the claim to multi-hop training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Reward Hacking Audit for Shaped Turn Rewards over Long Training
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as a search agent for 2000 updates with GRPO plus a turn reward from answer log-probability gain, and track correlation between mean turn reward and exact match on a held-out NQ and HotpotQA set at intervals of 100 updates. Inspect trajectories for degenerate behaviours: duplicate queries, answer leakage into the search query, and turn counts at the maximum. Run 5 seeds and report where the turn reward and exact match diverge, and test lowering the turn weight when they do.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; turn reward at 3 fixed weights; a variant that caps the turn reward at the outcome reward scale; a duplicate-query penalty.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Correlation stays positive through training and degenerate behaviours stay rare under the capped variant, appearing mainly when the weight is high. It fails if exact match falls late in training while turn reward keeps rising, showing the signal drifts from the final objective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Anchoring Check of Turn Rewards on a Held-Out Question Type
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct as a search agent with GRPO plus a turn reward from answer log-probability gain on NQ questions, with 8 rollouts, 3 seeds, and 6 turn weights. Evaluate exact match on NQ, TriviaQA, PopQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Musique, and track the turn reward against exact match on that set. Inspect trajectories for duplicate queries, answer text copied into search queries, and turn counts at the maximum, and report which weight keeps the turn reward and exact match aligned on that set.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; turn reward at 3 fixed weights; a variant that caps the turn reward at the outcome reward scale; a duplicate-query penalty.
COST: 3000
PREDICTION: Moderate weights keep the turn reward aligned with exact match on all sets, while high weights lead to answer copying into queries. It fails if alignment breaks on the multi-hop sets even at low weight, which would mean anchoring does not transfer beyond NQ.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Overhead Measurement of Turn Rewards in Group-Based Optimization
PROPOSAL: Measure the added cost of computing the turn reward in GRPO training of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as a search agent on NQ and HotpotQA questions. Instrument wall-clock per update for rollout generation, reward computation and the policy update, with 8 rollouts per query and 8 seeds, and compare against outcome-only GRPO. Report the percentage overhead of the forced-answer forward passes, excluding the first 10 updates as warm-up, and its share when the answer prefix is cached, plus exact match on HotpotQA to confirm that the cached version gives the same accuracy.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; turn reward with an uncached forward pass; turn reward with cached prefix; a learned process reward model as a costly reference.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Cached turn rewards add a few percent to update time and match the uncached version in exact match. It fails if the added passes grow with trajectory length enough to exceed ten percent, which would contradict the negligible-overhead requirement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn Reward Overhead and Accuracy at Two Backbone Sizes
PROPOSAL: Compare outcome-only GRPO with GRPO plus an answer-likelihood turn reward for Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct search agents trained on NQ and HotpotQA questions, with 8 rollouts per query. Instrument time per update for rollouts, reward computation and the policy update, over 5 seeds, and report exact match on the test benchmarks alongside the overhead. Report the percentage overhead for both sizes with a cached answer prefix and the ratio between sizes, and compare with a process reward model as a costly reference.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; turn reward without caching; turn reward with caching; a learned process reward model as a costly reference.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: The overhead stays at a few percent for both sizes and exact match improves at both. It fails if the overhead is larger for the bigger model, which would suggest the claim of negligible overhead holds only for small backbones.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn Reward Weight Schedule Versus Constant Weight
PROPOSAL: Compare a constant weight with a weight that decays over training for the turn reward added to GRPO advantages, using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as a search agent trained on NQ and HotpotQA questions with 8 rollouts per query. The decay anneals the weight to zero over 600 updates so the final objective dominates late training. Run 3 seeds per schedule and report exact match on NQ, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA and Bamboogle, the training reward curves, and the share of turns with positive reward through training.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; constant turn weight at 2 values; a schedule that grows the weight instead of decaying it; turn reward only in the first 200 updates.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The decaying schedule matches or beats the best constant weight on exact match while keeping late training anchored to the outcome. It fails if the growing schedule does as well, which would mean timing of the signal does not matter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn Reward Variants Compared on Search Agent Backbones
PROPOSAL: Compare 3 turn reward variants added to GRPO advantages: answer log-probability gain, rank of the gold answer among sampled answers, and a combination of both, on Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct trained on NQ and HotpotQA with 8 rollouts per query and 5 seeds. Report exact match on the test benchmarks, rank the variants by exact match averaged over backbones and by seed variance, the training reward curves, and the share of turns with positive reward by variant.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; the turn reward variants on their own; the combined variant at mixing weights set on validation; a random turn score.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: The combined variant matches or beats the separate variants on exact match over backbones, and the gain shrinks as the backbone grows. It fails if all 3 variants are indistinguishable, in which case the choice of turn signal does not matter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparison with Process-Reward Baselines on Multi-Hop Search
PROPOSAL: Compare outcome-only GRPO, GRPO with an answer-likelihood turn reward, and GRPO with a tree-search value estimate from 8 branches per turn with 3 sampled answers per branch, on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct search agents trained on NQ and HotpotQA with 8 rollouts per query. Evaluate exact match on NQ, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, Musique and Bamboogle, with 5 seeds. Report exact match against the number of generated tokens, to see whether turn rewards give an advantage over the tree-search estimate at equal token use.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; tree-search value estimate; a learned process reward model on gold evidence passages; turn reward with a shuffled answer prefix.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: The answer-likelihood reward matches the tree-search estimate in exact match at far fewer tokens, and both beat outcome-only training. It fails if the tree-search estimate wins at equal token use, which would limit the turn reward to the low-token regime.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn Rewards on a Hard Subset with Weak Backbones
PROPOSAL: Select the 3000 hardest training queries by outcome failure rate, and train weak search agents on them with GRPO plus an answer-likelihood turn reward, with 16 rollouts per query. Train Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct for 3 seeds apiece, and compare with outcome-only GRPO and with the same agents trained on a random query subset. Evaluate exact match on the test benchmarks, and report how the turn reward changes the share of queries with nonzero advantage.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; a random query subset of the same size; a learned process reward model on gold evidence passages; turn reward with a shuffled answer prefix.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: Turn rewards lift exact match on the hard subset where outcome-only GRPO stalls, and the random subset shows a smaller gain. It fails if outcome-only GRPO catches up after longer training, which would mean the turn reward only speeds up the early phase.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablating Turn Reward Components on a Small Search Agent
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct as a search agent on 2000 HotpotQA training questions with GRPO, and ablate 2 parts of the turn reward: the forced answer prefix used to compute log-probability, and the clipping of negative gains. Run 3 seeds per variant and evaluate exact match on 500 HotpotQA dev questions and 300 Bamboogle questions. Report the share of turns with positive reward and the correlation between turn reward and the final answer correctness at the level of whole trajectories.
CONTROLS: Full turn reward; no clipping; no answer prefix, using the generated answer instead; outcome-only GRPO; shuffled turn rewards.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Removing the answer prefix hurts most because the reward then depends on the generated answer, and clipping has a smaller effect. It fails if all variants match the full reward, showing the components do not matter at this scale.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Turn Reward Calibration over Query Types on 7B Search Agents
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as a search agent on NQ, TriviaQA and HotpotQA training questions with GRPO and an answer-likelihood turn reward, 8 rollouts per query, 8 seeds. Evaluate exact match on 6 test benchmarks, and analyse the share of turns with positive reward and the correlation between turn reward and answer correctness at the trajectory level, split by number of turns, question type and retrieval hit rate. Report calibration curves of turn reward against final correctness per split. Report the share of queries with a nonzero advantage per training stage.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; a variant with clipped negative gains; a variant without the forced answer prefix; shuffled turn rewards.
COST: 80
PREDICTION: Turn rewards correlate positively with final correctness at all splits, and calibration is better on multi-hop questions with more turns. It fails if the correlation vanishes for short trajectories, which would show the signal informs only long search sessions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Agreement Between Intrinsic Turn Rewards and Gold Supporting Facts
PROPOSAL: Take 500 HotpotQA training questions with annotated supporting facts and roll out Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct search agents with 8 trajectories per query. Label a turn as productive when its retrieved passages contain a supporting fact, then measure how well the answer-likelihood turn reward separates productive from unproductive turns with area under the ROC curve and rank correlation. Break the results down by turn index and by trajectory outcome, over 5 rollout seeds. The annotation is used only to evaluate the reward, never to train the agent.
CONTROLS: Random turn scores; passage overlap with the gold answer string; turn score from retrieval rank alone; a length-only score.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The turn reward separates productive from unproductive turns clearly better than chance and than length, with weaker separation on the last turn. It fails if passage overlap with the gold string separates as well, which would make the likelihood signal a costly proxy for string matching.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training Search Agents with Gold Supporting Facts or Intrinsic Turn Rewards
PROPOSAL: Train Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct search agents on 4000 HotpotQA training questions with annotated supporting facts, using GRPO with 8 rollouts per query and 3 variants: outcome only, outcome plus a supporting-fact hit reward per turn, and outcome plus the answer-likelihood turn reward. Evaluate exact match on HotpotQA dev and 2WikiMultiHopQA over 3 seeds, and compare the turn-level signals by how often a rewarded turn retrieved a supporting fact. Compare training time and exact match of the variants after the same number of updates. Break the exact match results down by the number of hops in the question.
CONTROLS: Outcome-only GRPO; random turn scores; turn score from retrieval rank alone; a length-only score.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The intrinsic reward reaches exact match close to the supporting-fact reward without annotation, and both beat outcome-only training. It fails if the supporting-fact reward clearly wins, which would show annotation still buys accuracy.
